item.title: Leveraging AI in Public Services: Opportunities, Risks and Implications for Governance and Accountability
item.content:encoded:
Wei Qian, Adelaide University

Cherrie Yang, Massey University

Pawan Adhikari, University of Essex

Ataur Belal, The University of Birmingham

Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming how public sector organisations deliver services and demonstrate accountability. While AI offers opportunities to improve efficiency, it presents significant governance challenges including obscured responsibility, reproduced biases, and gaps in existing accountability arrangements.

The special issue addresses AI as a socio-organisational phenomenon reshaping public sector accounting and governance. It welcomes interdisciplinary research from diverse contexts, particularly developing countries and perspectives challenging Western-centric approaches. Research should explore how AI impacts budgeting, professional identities, algorithmic bias, citizen co-production of accountability, and locally adapted practices, especially regarding responsibility when AI-informed decisions harm marginalised communities.

Appel publié par Financial Accountability and Management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • AI transforming public service accounting and public value generation
  • AI reshaping public budgeting and resource allocation
  • Skills and professional identities in AI-enabled public services
  • Governance and measurement tools through predictive analytics and automated decision systems
  • AI and demand-side versus plural forms of public accountability
  • Accountability relationships reconfigured by AI
  • Citizens and beneficiaries co-producing accountability with AI
  • Responsibility and accountability for adverse AI-informed outcomes
  • Algorithmic bias and data inequalities in public accountability
  • AI governance and institutional power relations in public service accounting
  • Locally developed or adapted AI practices and alternative understandings of public value
  • AI risks to local communities and marginalised constituents

Timeline

  • August 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: AI, Policy and Public Value: Theorising the reciprocal relationship between AI and policy and its implications for public value
item.content:encoded:
Nisreen Ameen, University of Reading

Federico Iannacci, University of Sussex

Daniel Gozman, University of Sydney

James S. Denford, Royal Military College of Canada

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence embedded in public services shapes and is shaped by policy, and how these interactions affect public value. It addresses the bidirectional relationship between AI and policy: AI influences how policy problems are framed and implemented, while policy decisions configure how AI systems are developed and deployed.

The special issue invites Information Systems research that theorises AI as central to policy formation and enactment. It seeks to understand how organisations translate AI-policy ambitions into practice, how governance mechanisms enable accountability, and how these processes create, distribute or undermine public value—understood as plural, contested outcomes encompassing efficiency, equity, participation and welfare.

All submissions must include dedicated policy implications derived from evidence and analysis. Research should address how AI-mediated practices affect citizens and marginalised groups, and what trade-offs arise between competing values.

Appel publié par Information Systems Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Creation and Distribution of Public Value
  • AI Use and the Production of Policy
  • AI Governance Beyond Regulatory Compliance
  • Policy Translation and Organisational Capability
  • Participation, Inequality and Contestation
  • IS Knowledge and Policy Formation

Timeline

  • June 15, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Public management and public value in geoeconomic governance
item.content:encoded:
Javier Cifuentes-Faura, University of Murcia

Governments worldwide are increasingly using economic tools such as trade policy, industrial policy, and strategic investments to advance geopolitical objectives, a phenomenon known as geoeconomic statecraft. However, research has largely focused on geopolitical and economic outcomes, leaving a significant gap in understanding how public organizations manage, finance, and evaluate these interventions.

This special issue addresses this gap by examining public management and public value implications of geoeconomic governance. As governments take on roles as investors, market participants, and coordinators of critical sectors, public organizations face challenges in balancing transparency with security, efficiency with resilience, and fiscal discipline with long-term strategic goals. The issue seeks contributions exploring how public value should be defined when economic, security, and societal objectives compete.

Appel publié par Public Money & Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Public management of geoeconomic strategies and strategic state interventions
  • Public value creation and distribution in geoeconomic governance
  • Public financial management of strategic economic interventions
  • Accountability and performance management in geoeconomic and mission-oriented public policies
  • Governance and management of strategic public investments
  • Administrative capacity for managing geoeconomic risks and strategic industries
  • Fiscal governance and accountability of industrial subsidies and strategic investments
  • Transparency, oversight, and accountability in strategic public procurement
  • Public sector governance of strategic infrastructure and critical sectors
  • Measuring and evaluating public value in strategic economic interventions
  • Public management of economic sanctions and export controls
  • Governance of critical supply chains and strategic dependencies
  • Accountability in sovereign wealth funds and state-owned enterprises
  • Governance of national security-related public expenditure
  • Investment screening and public sector accountability
  • Multi-level governance of strategic economic policies
  • Public–private partnerships in strategically important sectors
  • Institutional and organizational responses to geopolitical and economic uncertainty
  • Comparative public management approaches to geoeconomic governance

Timeline

  • December 30, 2027: Manuscript deadline for research articles and new development pieces
  • March 1, 2028: Manuscript deadline for debate pieces

item.title: Generative AI and Data Envelopment Analysis for Performance Measurement and Public Value
item.content:encoded:
This special issue explores the intersection of generative artificial intelligence and data envelopment analysis as tools for measuring organizational performance and creating public value. The collection seeks research that demonstrates how these technologies can enhance performance evaluation methodologies and provide insights into efficiency across various sectors, particularly in public organizations where value creation extends beyond traditional financial metrics.

Appel publié par Socio-Economic Planning Sciences. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Applications of generative AI in performance measurement
  • Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) methodologies
  • Public value creation and assessment
  • Integration of AI and DEA techniques
  • Performance evaluation in public sector organizations
  • Efficiency measurement using advanced analytics

Timeline

  • September 1, 2026: Submission deadline
